Formula sheet ​

A working reference, not a derivation. Every entry states its assumptions. If you use a formula outside those assumptions, you own the error.

Conventions

  • Quaternions are scalar-last: q=[x,y,z,w], matching three.js.
  • Rotation matrices are active and map a vector from the body frame to the reference frame: vR=RR←BvB.
  • Angles are radians unless a degree symbol appears.
  • Time is seconds unless stated. Mission time has an epoch and a scale.
  • Specific impulse Isp is in seconds; use g0=9.80665 m/s2 only for the rocket equation.

Geometry and trigonometry ​

QuantityFormula
Vector norm‖v‖=vx2+vy2+vz2
Dot producta⋅b=‖a‖‖b‖cos⁡θ
Cross product magnitude‖a×b‖=‖a‖‖b‖sin⁡θ
Angle between vectorsθ=atan2(‖a×b‖, a⋅b)
Rotation about unit axis n^v′=vcos⁡θ+(n^×v)sin⁡θ+n^(n^⋅v)(1−cos⁡θ)
Small-angle approximationsin⁡θ≈θ, cos⁡θ≈1−θ2/2

Use atan2 for angles. acos loses precision near 0 and 180° and cannot tell left from right.

Frames and rotation matrices ​

Elementary rotations ​

Rx(ϕ)=[1000cos⁡ϕ−sin⁡ϕ0sin⁡ϕcos⁡ϕ],Ry(θ)=[cos⁡θ0sin⁡θ010−sin⁡θ0cos⁡θ],Rz(ψ)=[cos⁡ψ−sin⁡ψ0sin⁡ψcos⁡ψ0001].

Composition ​

For a 3-2-1 (yaw–pitch–roll) sequence:

R=Rz(ψ)Ry(θ)Rx(ϕ).

Matrix multiplication is not commutative. The order is part of the convention and must be documented.

Inverse and transpose ​

Rotation matrices are orthonormal:

R−1=RT,detR=+1.

To go the other way, transpose. Do not invert numerically unless you are debugging a non-orthonormal matrix.

Earth-fixed to inertial (approximation) ​

For a body-fixed vector rF and rotation rate ω:

rI=Rz(θGHA)rF,r˙I=r˙F+ω×rF.

For the Moon, replace the rotation angle and rate with lunar values. "GHA" is replaced by the lunar body-fixed rotation angle at the epoch.

Direction cosine matrix propagation ​

R˙=R[ωB]×,[ω]×=[0−ωzωyωz0−ωx−ωyωx0].

This is the continuous-time attitude kinematics in matrix form. It is equivalent to the quaternion form below but has more states and needs re-orthonormalization.

Quaternions ​

Definition and normalization ​

q=[x,y,z,w]=[vsin⁡(θ/2),cos⁡(θ/2)],‖q‖=1.

The rotation angle is θ=2arccos⁡(w) and the axis is n^=v/‖v‖.

Multiplication ​

With q1=[v1,w1] and q2=[v2,w2]:

q1⊗q2=[w1v2+w2v1+v1×v2w1w2−v1⋅v2].

The order matters. q1⊗q2 applies q2 first, then q1 when rotating a vector.

Rotating a vector ​

v′=qvq∗,q∗=[−v,w].

Quaternion to matrix (body to reference) ​

R(q)=[1−2(y2+z2)2(xy−wz)2(xz+wy)2(xy+wz)1−2(x2+z2)2(yz−wx)2(xz−wy)2(yz+wx)1−2(x2+y2)].

Attitude kinematics ​

For body rates ωB:

q˙=12q⊗[ωB0].

In component form:

x˙=12(wωx+yωz−zωy),y˙=12(wωy+zωx−xωz),z˙=12(wωz+xωy−yωx),w˙=−12(xωx+yωy+zωz).

Renormalize after integration. For a first-order step at rate ω over dt, the exact update is

qk+1=qk⊗[ω^sin⁡(‖ω‖dt/2)cos⁡(‖ω‖dt/2)].

Quaternion error and sign ​

The relative rotation is qerr=qref∗⊗q. Choose the sign so that w≥0; otherwise the controller takes the long way around. A common bug: two quaternions representing the same attitude with opposite signs produce a 360° error.

Euler angles from a 3-2-1 matrix ​

ϕ=atan2(R32,R33),θ=−arcsin⁡(R31),ψ=atan2(R21,R11).

Gimbal lock occurs at θ=±90°. Do not use Euler angles as the primary attitude state.

Rigid-body dynamics ​

Newton–Euler ​

mv˙=F,Iω˙+ω×(Iω)=τ.

Both are written in an inertial frame for translation and in the body frame for rotation. Mixing them is a classic error.

Mass flow and thrust ​

m˙=−TIspg0,T=m˙Ispg0.

For a throttle fraction u∈[0,1] and maximum thrust Tmax:

T=uTmax,m˙=−uTmaxIspg0.

Rocket equation ​

Δv=Ispg0ln⁡(m0mf),m0mf=exp⁡(ΔvIspg0).

Inertia ​

For a point mass at distance r: I=mr2. For a uniform solid cylinder of mass m, radius r, length L about its axis: I=12mr2. About a transverse axis through the centre: I=112m(3r2+L2).

The inertia tensor is symmetric and positive definite. In the principal axes frame it is diagonal. If mass changes, inertia changes; if you ignore that, the controller gain is wrong at the end of the burn.

Gravity ​

g(r)=−μr3r,g(r)=μr2.

At the lunar surface, g=1.624 m/s2. At 15 km altitude, g=1.597 m/s2.

Hover and thrust-to-weight ​

Thover=mg,TWR=Tmaxmg.

Hover throttle is uhover=1/TWR. A TWR of 2 means half throttle hovers; a TWR below 1 means the vehicle cannot leave the surface.

Control ​

PID ​

u(t)=Kpe(t)+Ki∫0te(τ)dτ+Kdde(t)dt.

Discrete form with sample time Δt:

uk=Kpek+KiΔt∑j=0kej+KdΔt(ek−ek−1).

Use derivative-on-measurement to avoid derivative kick when the setpoint changes. Clamp the integral (anti-windup) and the output.

Second-order response ​

For a canonical second-order system

y¨+2ζωny˙+ωn2y=ωn2r,
QuantityFormula
Natural frequencyωn
Damping ratioζ
Peak overshootexp⁡(−πζ/1−ζ2)
Settling time (2%)≈4/(ζωn)
Rise time (10–90%)≈1.8/ωn for ζ≈0.7
Phase marginrelated to ζ; roughly ζ≈PM/100 for PM in degrees

A sampled controller needs ωn≪ωs/10 as a starting rule, where ωs=2πfs. If the mode you are trying to control is near Nyquist, no gain tuning will save it.

LQR ​

For x˙=Ax+Bu and cost

J=∫0∞(xTQx+uTRu)dt,

the optimal gain is K=R−1BTP, where P solves the continuous algebraic Riccati equation:

ATP+PA−PBR−1BTP+Q=0.

For discrete time, use the discrete Riccati equation and uk=−Kxk. Tune Q and R by units and priority, not by random search. Check closed-loop poles and actuator saturation.

Discretization ​

MethodApproximationNote
Forward Eulers≈(z−1)/TsCan be unstable for fast poles
Backward Eulers≈(z−1)/(zTs)Stable mapping, adds damping
Tustin (bilinear)s≈2Tsz−1z+1Good default; pre-warp if needed
ZOHexact for a zero-order holdUse when the plant model is available

Orbital mechanics ​

Two-body motion ​

r¨=−μr3r,ε=v22−μr,h=r×v.

Vis-viva ​

v2=μ(2r−1a).

Circular orbit ​

vc=μr,T=2πa3μ.

Escape ​

vesc=2μr.

Conic geometry ​

r=p1+ecos⁡ν,p=a(1−e2),rp=a(1−e),ra=a(1+e).

Delta-v for a plane change ​

Δv=2vsin⁡(Δi2).

Hohmann transfer (two impulses, coplanar circular orbits) ​

Δv1=μr1(2r2r1+r2−1),Δv2=μr2(1−2r1r1+r2).ttransfer=πat3μ,at=r1+r22.

Navigation and estimation ​

Kalman filter ​

Predict:

x^−=Fx^+Bu,P−=FPFT+Q.

Update:

K=P−HT(HP−HT+R)−1,x^=x^−+K(z−Hx^−),P=(I−KH)P−.

Innovation and consistency ​

y=z−Hx^−,S=HP−HT+R,NIS=yTS−1y.

For a correctly tuned filter with n measurements, the normalized innovation squared should have a mean near n. If NIS is consistently much larger, the filter is overconfident (too small Q or R); if much smaller, it is underconfident. Test this over many runs, not one.

Continuous propagation ​

x˙=f(x,u),P˙=FP+PFT+Q.

The state transition matrix over Δt is approximately F≈I+AΔt for small steps, or use a matrix exponential for a linear system.

Quaternion error for the filter ​

Use a small-angle error quaternion δq≈[12δθ,1] and estimate the 3-vector δθ. This keeps the covariance 3×3 instead of 4×4 with a norm constraint.

Sensor noise ​

QuantityFormula
Varianceσ2
Standard deviationσ
White-noise densityQc with units of (unit)²/Hz
Discrete process noiseQ≈QcΔt for a simple random walk
Averaging N samplesσavg=σ/N

Check the convention: some texts define Q as a density, some as a per-step covariance. A factor of Δt changes the tuning completely.

Allan variance (sensor characterization) ​

For gyro bias instability and random walk, plot Allan deviation versus averaging time. The minimum of the curve gives the bias instability; the slope at long averaging times gives the random walk. Use it to set Q, not a guess from a datasheet.

Statistics and Monte Carlo ​

QuantityFormula
Meanx¯=1N∑xi
Sample variances2=1N−1∑(xi−x¯)2
Standard error of the meanSE=s/N
95% interval (normal)x¯±1.96SE
Percentilesort, then interpolate at rank p(N−1)
3σ coverage (normal, 1D)99.73%
3σ coverage (normal, 3D)about 97.0% for a chi-square with 3 degrees of freedom

The last row is a common interview trap: a 3D position error inside a 3σ radial ellipsoid is not the same probability as a 1D 3σ. State which one you mean.

For a Monte Carlo with N runs, the standard error of an estimated probability p is p(1−p)/N. To resolve a 1% failure probability with reasonable confidence, you need hundreds to thousands of runs, not 20.

Propellant and mass ​

m(t)=m0−∫0tm˙(τ)dτ,Δv=∫Tmdt.

For a constant thrust and mass flow:

Δv=Ispg0ln⁡(m0m0−m˙t).

Reserve fraction:

reserve=mprop,available−mprop,requiredmprop,required.

State whether the reserve is a percentage of the required propellant, the total load, or the landing mass. Teams routinely mean different things.

Check yourself

A teammate computes a 3D position error and says it is '3σ, so 99.73% of cases are inside.' What is wrong?

Check yourself

You change the control loop from 100 Hz to 20 Hz but keep the same continuous gains. What is the most likely result?

Resources ​

  • Vallado, Fundamentals of Astrodynamics and Applications — the reference for the orbital section.
  • NASA Reference Publication 1311: Quaternion FAQ — conventions and pitfalls.
  • Schaub & Junkins, Analytical Mechanics of Space Systems — rigid-body dynamics and control.
  • Maybeck, Stochastic Models, Estimation, and Control — the Kalman filter foundations.
  • NIST Engineering Statistics Handbook — Monte Carlo and interval interpretation.
